entry.title: New page: How to use Jev with Codex, OpenCode, Cursor and Hermes Agent (TypeSafe AI). Of 18 Jev coding-agent integrations read in source, 1 is vendor-published (OpenClaw) and none comes from TypeSafe; 6 act on Jev's answer, and 4 of those let the tool call run when Jev errors.

New page: Jev 1.13 and jev-latest (TypeSafe AI): model IDs and aliases by route. On 4 of 6 routes read on 6 Oct 2026 you can write a versioned Jev ID; Vercel and Cloudflare take only an unversioned one. jev-latest points to jev-1.13.0 on TypeSafe's models page.

When Jev fails updated: of 58 Jev implementations read in source, 32 stop or hold the action when Jev errors and 7 let it through unchecked: 4 content-moderation bots, 2 agent hooks and one Spring AI passage filter. New Coding agents domain (10 use cases); copyable checklist regenerated.

Claude Code and MCP: two guard rows added. jev-permission-gate falls back to Claude Code's built-in classifier when Jev fails; jev-llm-guard only returns a verdict (its CLI exits 0 whatever the verdict). Both are at the commits read on 4 Oct.
Products recounted on 6 Oct 2026: 92 rows (A 75, B 16, C 1), with 20 coding-agent and guard rows added; none independently verified in production.

Vercel AI Gateway lists two providers for Jev (checked 6 Oct 2026, 05:15 UTC): TypeSafe AI (zero data retention) and DigitalOcean (no zero data retention). Vercel picks a provider by uptime and latency unless you set the provider order.

Drift notes: LiteLLM 1.104.0 keeps the Jev classifier's failure path unchanged from 8d28e8d; no new release of the six framework packages; ai 7.0.128 and @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai 3.0.13 are patch releases, not re-audited.

Access status rechecked 6 Oct 2026, 05:15 UTC: unchanged (signups open, no new-user credit, API operational). Price, listed limits, model aliases (jev-latest and jev-preview point to jev-1.13.0) and the subprocessor list unchanged; the API's 90-day uptime moved from 99.829% to 99.826% with no new incident listed.

Failure colours made the same on every page that shows a failure verdict: green fail-closed or held, red fail-open or acts-anyway, blue fallback, amber advisory, gray no-decision, white not recorded or no threshold. Recoloured: Claude Code and MCP, support-ticket triage, model routing, content moderation, email sorting, trading and fraud gates, browser and computer use, n8n, Products, the Use cases hub and the errors page. AutoModeMiddleware now links its pinned commit 4af7ab8 instead of PyPI.

New page: Jev browser use and computer use (TypeSafe AI). Of 7 Jev browser and computer-use agents read in source, none clicks or types when Jev errors, but 5 act on low-confidence answers, and only 1 asks a person before send, buy or delete.

New page: Jev LangChain and other framework integrations (TypeSafe AI). Of 6 Jev framework packages read in source, 4 are pre-1.0 and none comes from TypeSafe; 4 raise Jev errors to your code, while the community Spring AI filter passes passages through unscreened.

New section on Where to use: Jev is not listed in the Amazon Bedrock model catalog or the Azure AI Foundry model catalog (checked 5 Oct 2026, 05:18–05:19 UTC), and TypeSafe's docs do not mention either. Call TypeSafe's API or a gateway.

When Jev fails updated: of 51 Jev implementations in 9 use cases read in source, 30 stop or hold the action when Jev errors and 6 let it through unchecked: 4 content-moderation bots, one Claude Code hook and one Spring AI passage filter. Adds 8 browser and 4 framework rows and a copyable checklist.

Products refreshed: 72 rows (A 55, B 16, C 1); Jev for Chrome, computer-use-jev and jev-android upgraded from B to A; 5 new grade-A browser rows; six framework packages listed as not counted. 0 independently verified in production.

Small additions: Strands Decider 2B on Alternatives (benchmark and AWS attribution Reported), a Zapier note on the n8n page, an EU-hosting line on data privacy, and tool-documentation links on Jev as a judge. Rate-limit check dates moved to 5 Oct.

Corrections: langchain-typesafe 0.0.1a3 was uploaded on 20 Sep 2026, not 4 Oct; @effect/ai-typesafe is 4.0.1; the Spring AI integration is a community package; the AndroidWorld paper (arXiv 2609.30186) was submitted on 24 Sep. The Python page notes that the Pydantic AI Gateway did not list TypeSafe on 5 Oct.

Access status rechecked 5 Oct 2026, 05:13 UTC: unchanged (signups open, no new-user credit, API operational). Price, limits and the subprocessor list unchanged; the API's 90-day uptime moved from 99.826% to 99.829%. Check dates updated on Home, access status and the cost worksheet.

New page: Jev trading bot and fraud gates (TypeSafe AI). Of 4 Jev trading bots read in source, 2 can still place a new order when Jev errors; all 4 can trade without Jev. None of 3 fraud or payment gates moves money. In two bots "mock" means no Jev, not no trading. No advice and no performance figures.

New page: When Jev fails (TypeSafe AI). Of 39 Jev implementations read in source, 21 stop or hold the action when Jev errors and 5 let it through unchecked: 4 content-moderation bots and one Claude Code hook. Counts per condition and use case with "not recorded" counts, and an 8-question checklist.

New page: Jev as a judge (TypeSafe AI). Of 4 Jev judge tools read in source, DeepEval stops the run on a Jev error; the other 3 drop the item from the score, and openlayer jevals still reports it as passed. Judge studies B02, B06 and B08 copied unchanged.
